original_question: Determine whether the bound 2.25*k^2 is the best possible general upper bound for the Stanley-Wilf limit of a classical permutation pattern of length k.
target_in_paper: Section 4, “Are layered patterns the most easily avoided?”, especially the discussion on pp. 247–248 that first recalls the conjecture that, among patterns of a fixed length k, the largest Stanley-Wilf limit is attained by some layered pattern, and then notes that Bóna’s improved bound 2.25 k^2 would therefore be a universal bound, while adding that it is unknown whether this bound is best possible.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right local topic in the paper: a universal upper bound for the Stanley-Wilf limit of classical patterns of fixed length k, the specific coefficient 2.25, and the issue of whether that coefficient is optimal.
missing_details: In arXiv:1210.7320, the bound 2.25 k^2 is not presented as an unconditional theorem for all classical patterns of length k; it becomes a universal bound only under the nearby conjecture that the largest Stanley-Wilf limit among patterns of length k is attained by a layered pattern.

The paper’s asymptotic quantity should be defined explicitly: for a classical pattern τ, the Stanley-Wilf limit is L(τ) = lim_{n→∞} Av_τ(n)^{1/n}, where Av_τ(n) is the number of permutations of length n avoiding τ.
The quantifiers should be explicit: the question concerns every positive integer k and every classical pattern τ of length k.
The phrase “best possible general upper bound” should be made precise as asking whether the coefficient 2.25 can be lowered in a universal bound of the form L(τ) ≤ C k^2 for all τ of length k.
The paper’s surrounding discussion is specifically about classical permutation patterns; it should not drift to vincular, bivincular, mesh, or class-based variants.
The nearby section also discusses which layered pattern might be extremal, but that is a separate issue and should not be folded into this question.
refined_question: For every positive integer k, assume that among all classical permutation patterns of length k, the maximum Stanley-Wilf limit is attained by a layered pattern. If L(τ) = lim_{n→∞} Av_τ(n)^{1/n} denotes the Stanley-Wilf limit of a classical pattern τ ∈ S_k, is the resulting universal bound L(τ) ≤ 2.25 k^2 optimal, or can the coefficient 2.25 be reduced in a bound that holds for all classical patterns of length k?
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft because Section 4 is exactly where Steingrímsson discusses the conjecture that the extremal Stanley-Wilf limit at fixed length k is attained by a layered pattern (p. 247), then records Bóna’s improved layered-pattern bound 2.25 k^2 and immediately remarks that, if the layered-pattern conjecture is true, this would bound the Stanley-Wilf limit of any pattern of length k, but that it is unknown whether this bound is best possible (p. 248). To make the question stand-alone, one must also import the paper’s definition of the Stanley-Wilf limit from Section 3 (p. 245).
